hook.line: Tomás is writing the cooperative's newsletter about the restoration, and he wants to say exactly when things happened and what came right after what. Plain *cuando* is too vague for that.
hook.en: As soon as Vale arrives, we'll start.

examples.es: Nada más llegar Tomás al café, se fue la luz.
examples.en: As soon as Tomás got to the café, the power went out.
We had barely opened when Hernando arrived.

examples.es: En cuanto vi la viga, supe que estaba rota.
examples.en: As soon as I saw the beam, I knew it was broken.
As soon as Vale arrives, we'll start.

examples.es: Una vez que termine la obra, abrimos el café.
examples.en: Once the work is finished, we'll open the café.

examples.es: A medida que avanzaba la noche, llegaba más gente.
examples.en: As the night went on, more people arrived.

rule:
Spanish has precise little openers for "when", each with its own job.

*Nada más* + infinitive: "the moment that". *Nada más llegar Tomás* has no *-ed* ending and no "he": the infinitive carries it.
*Apenas* + past: "barely had we... when". It is quick and sudden.
*En cuanto* and *una vez que*: "as soon as", "once". About the past, use a normal past verb (*En cuanto vi*). About the future, use the "wish" form of the verb: *En cuanto llegue*, *una vez que termine*. English says "arrives" and "is finished"; Spanish uses this special form, never a future (*llegará* is wrong here).
*A medida que*: "as", while something keeps growing or changing. Never *a medida de que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these temporal conjunctions. After *en cuanto* and *una vez que* about the future, the verb is in the present subjunctive (*llegue*, *termine*).

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence. You mean "as soon as Vale arrives", in the future: ___ Vale, empezamos. (en cuanto llegue / en cuanto llegó)
yourTurn.why: It is about the future, so Spanish uses the "wish" form *llegue*, not a future or a past.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose and type: "As soon as Tomás got there, the power went out." Nada más ___ Tomás, se fue la luz. (llegar / llegó)
yourTurn.answer: Nada más llegar Tomás, se fue la luz.
accept: Nada más llegar Tomás al café, se fue la luz.
yourTurn.why: *Nada más* is followed by the infinitive, with the person right after it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "As the night went on, more people arrived."
yourTurn.answer: A medida que avanzaba la noche, llegaba más gente.
accept: Llegaba más gente a medida que avanzaba la noche.
yourTurn.why: *A medida que* + imperfect describes something that keeps changing while time goes on.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "Once the work is finished, we'll open the café."
yourTurn.answer: Una vez que termine la obra, abrimos el café.
accept: Una vez que termine la obra, vamos a abrir el café.
Una vez que termine la obra, abriremos el café.
yourTurn.why: About the future, *una vez que* takes the "wish" form, *termine*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "We had barely opened when Hernando arrived."
yourTurn.why: *Apenas* + a past verb gives the quick "barely had we... when" feeling.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about the past: *En cuanto llegue Vale, empezamos.* It happened yesterday. Say it with *llegó* and *empezamos*.
yourTurn.why: Once it has already happened, *en cuanto* takes an ordinary past verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "As soon as I saw the beam, I knew it was broken."
yourTurn.answer: En cuanto vi la viga, supe que estaba rota.
yourTurn.why: A finished past event after *en cuanto* uses a normal past verb.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *en cuanto* about the future, Spanish uses *llegue*, never the future tense.

pitfalls.wrong: Nada más Tomás llegó, se fue la luz.
pitfalls.right: Nada más llegar Tomás, se fue la luz.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Nada más* wants the infinitive, then the person.

pitfalls.wrong: A medida de que avanzaba la noche, llegaba más gente.
pitfalls.right: A medida que avanzaba la noche, llegaba más gente.
pitfalls.why: The set phrase is *a medida que*, with no *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Una vez que terminará la obra, abrimos el café.
pitfalls.right: Una vez que termine la obra, abrimos el café.
pitfalls.why: Same rule as *en cuanto*: no future after *una vez que*, use *termine*.

personal: Tell us one true thing about your day: *En cuanto llego a casa,* and finish it.
